## Modelling approach

Here is how we will investigate the patient outcomes with various linear modelling strategies.

### Basic Model Setup

For every patient we have their 

1. demographic features :
   - `current_age`
   - `gender`
   - `ethnicity`
   - `religiosity`
   - `marriage status`
4. Other phenotypes
   - alcohol use disorder
   - substance use disorders
2. Patient Outcome, whether they were coded for 
   - SI 
   - Broad SA 
   - Narrow SA

### Parameter Comparisons

Most basic thing, run a glm with all features and look at betas + p-values + variance contributions for each model.
Basically just `summary(glm(outcome ~ demographics + has_alcohol_UD + has_substance_UD + history_features))`

### Bootstrapping

Ok, case/controls are very imbalanced, so can we apply bootstrapping, so for 10K bootstraps:

1. bootstrap pick ALL cases + same number of random controls
2. Run basic glm as specified above
3. tidy into neat tabel

Now look at bootstrap distributions and compute empirical p-values from unbalanced results above
